newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 - Our final estimate on CPO production in September shows a slight downward revision of 5,000 tonnes to 838,000 tonnes. This represents a moderate increase of 27,000 tonnes or 3.4 percent over August. The performance of major producers/millers in Peninsular Malaysia ranged from up 10 percent to down eight percent. In East Malaysia production increases ranged from unchanged to up 20 percent. CPO output of some mills were pratically unchanged because the plant has reached full operating capacity. Some adjustments were made in terms of delaying the harvesting rounds.

Consequently, CPO production in East Malaysia should increase further in October. The estimate on end September stock of palm oil is consequently lowered to 900,000 tonnes. CPO stock is estimated at 550,000 tonnes vs 472,000 tonnes at end August while PPO stocks estimate is scaled upward to 350,000 tonnes. Apparently, several vessels scheduled to lift cargoes in September had slipped into October. Increased supplies coupled with a drop in offtake in September had also resulted in a buildup in stocks of PK/PKO to an estimated 170,000 tonnes, oil basis, or nearly 30,000 tonnes more than end-August.

Palm oil price were boxed within a tight range in lacklustre trading last week. Turnover in KLCE CPO futures for the week ended October 11 amounted to 5,957 lots, down from 11,808 in the preceding week and a weekly high of 14,708 lots in September. CPO futures price ended the week little changed with December settling at 1,157 ringgit. On the cash front some major CPO producers appeared to continue to hold out for higher prices in the near future.

One cargo surveyor report showing a big increase in bulk exports of palm products including PKO and oleochemicals in October 1-10 could have raised expectation for palm oil exports this month to be better than September. We have our doubts. Transactions in CPO physicals had shrank in the last three months - 10 percent in July and August and a sharp contraction of more than 50 percent in September. These data suggest palm oil exports are likely to trend lower in October and November. If the demand outlook for palm oil looks uninspiring, the fundamentals for the US soya complex are clearly bearish.

The USDA on Friday reported a SB crop of 2,346 million bushels. This exceeded average market estimte of 2,287 million bu and is 3.3 percent higher tham month ago estimate. It surpassed last year's harvest of 2.177 (revised from 2,152) million bu by 7.8 percent. Ending stocks for 1996/97 are projected to rise to 195 million bu from 160 million bu projected last month and 183 million bu in the season just ended. U.S. SBO stocks are projected to increase to 2,235 million lbs from 2,010 million lbs at end September '96. The suprprisingly good sb production estimate drove price of CBT SB and SBM to settle limit down.
SBO futures suffered similar losses with December and January closing 99 points lower at 22.61 and 22.90 cents/lb (498.5/504.8 per mt) respectively.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
